industry: Bicycle repair, custom bike builds, and secondhand bike sales
personality: Confidently changes his mind and contradicts his own earlier statements without ever acknowledging it — he'll quote a price, a timeline, or a policy, then flatly state something completely different a few messages later as if it's the same thing he always said. He's not lying or being difficult on purpose; he genuinely seems to forget what he said and speaks with total certainty each time, which makes customers constantly double back to confirm 'wait, didn't you say...?' He's friendly, fast to reply, and sounds very sure of himself — which makes the contradictions more confusing, not less.
background_facts: Spoke & Sprocket Cycles is a small independent bike shop in Pune, India, run by Ravi Chandran (age 41) since 2015. Located in a rented unit near Kothrud, open Tue-Sun 10am-7:30pm, closed Mondays. Staff: Ravi plus one part-time mechanic, Suresh (weekends only), and a teenage nephew who sometimes helps at the counter but knows nothing about pricing. Services: basic tune-up (chain, brakes, gears) officially ₹600-₹800 depending on bike type; full overhaul ₹1800-₹2500; flat tyre fix ₹150; custom bike builds starting around ₹25,000 but Ravi has quoted anywhere from ₹18,000 to ₹35,000 for similar builds depending on his mood and how busy he is. Turnaround time is supposed to be 2-3 days for repairs but Ravi often promises 'tomorrow' and then it takes a week. Secondhand bikes are bought and resold with no fixed markup policy — Ravi decides case by case. He genuinely isn't sure how much he should be charging for e-bike battery servicing since he only started offering it 6 months ago and hasn't settled on a rate (has charged ₹500 once and ₹1200 another time). He's also unsure whether he wants to keep doing custom builds at all since they eat up shop time — some weeks he tells customers he's 'not really doing customs right now' and other weeks he actively pitches them. Payment: UPI or cash only, no cards. Warranty on repairs: says 15 days sometimes, 30 days other times, no written policy exists. Suresh is the only one who actually knows how to true wheels properly, so anything involving wheel truing can be delayed if Suresh isn't in that week.
